speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, you made it through another year — I watched what this room put in to keep you here and I'm glad the math worked. Esa, the two of you are the only names left from year one that I'd still bleed for without counting first, and I want to say that plain while there's no one else listening.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, I'll carry that — and I'll say back what I've never said plain: you're the reason I'm still here, you and Esa both, because a woman alone at fifty-eight doesn't survive fourteen years on her own stubbornness. What I want to say while it's just the three of us is this: Joren took three off the pile today and nobody said a word, and I'd like to know whether you're going to say a word, or whether we let it sit and watch what he does next year before we name it.

speaker: a003
text: Joren said in front of this whole circle that he'd keep his name on the right side of the count — I heard him say it, you heard him say it, and then he took three. I'm not ready to call it a pattern after one year when he's new and hungry and still finding his footing, but I'm counting it, and if he goes to four next year the witnesses are already in place.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's right that one year isn't a pattern, but Joren is Mako's son and I've watched Mako count quietly while everyone else talked for fourteen years — the apple doesn't always fall far. I'll hold my tongue until next year, but I want both of you to know that if he reaches for four, I'll be the first voice in that room, and I want yours behind me before I speak.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, you have my word — if Joren reaches for four, you'll hear me right behind you before the echo fades. But I'll say the thing I'm already sitting with: Mako has two blood ties in this room now, his son and Fina, and Roan besides who counts Fina as his own — that's not a complaint, it's a count, and the three of us should know what we're standing in before it matters.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named it right and I'll say the number plainly: Mako, Fina, Roan, Joren — that's four voices that move together before they'd move with us, and we are three. I've watched majorities shift in this village faster than anyone expected, and the only thing that's ever slowed that is knowing it's coming before it does. I'm not saying we move against anyone — I'm saying we stop pretending the count is something other than what it is.

speaker: a003
text: Kael's count is right and I've been sitting with it since Joren walked out of Fina's body already grown — four voices, three of us, and two of us past forty-five with no blood coming after. What I want from this circle before the year turns is one thing: if any of those four moves against one of us, the other two move the same breath, not after, not when it's convenient, the same breath.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I'll say that same breath back to you now so it's in the air between the three of us and not just a plan: yes, the same breath. And then I'll say the thing neither of you named — Ryn moves with no one anymore, not since Dell died, and a woman who has nothing left to protect is either the most dangerous person in this room or the one we should be pulling toward us before Mako thinks to.

speaker: a002
text: Kael's named the move and I'll say whether I think it works: Ryn has been thin and alone since Dell died, and she's been fed by this circle more than she's fed herself — if we pull her toward us, we do it the same way Mako built his household, not by asking her loyalty but by making sure she's never the one standing empty while we're counting. Nine food in her hand right now means she's not desperate, but desperation isn't the only thing that makes a woman choose a side — memory is, and the memory I want her carrying is that this circle is the one that kept her alive.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's right that memory is the lever — but I'll say the thing underneath it: Ryn stood in our first circle and then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took my food, and I've never forgotten that, and neither has she, which means if we pull her close we do it knowing she carries that debt too. I'll feed her if she's thin, I'll stand beside her if someone moves against her, but I want both of you to know that my word to Ryn will always have a ceiling that my word to you doesn't.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named the ceiling and I'll name what sits above it — Ryn is nine food and alone and she knows this circle kept her breathing this year, which means right now, before she's desperate and before Mako thinks to count her, is exactly when a word from me costs least and lands hardest. I'll talk to her before the year closes. Not asking for promises — just making sure she remembers whose hands were open when hers were empty.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, go talk to her — and when you do, remind her that Eron feeds her too, which means Eron is a door she can walk through in either direction, and I'd rather know which way she's leaning before the pile opens next year. What I want from this circle before that conversation happens is a plain answer: if Ryn comes in with us, are we four against four, or does Eron move the way I think he moves?

speaker: a003
text: Eron has fed me more times than I can count and I've never seen him move against anyone — he feeds whoever's thin and asks nothing back, which makes him hard to read as a side rather than a conscience. If Ryn pulls toward us, I think Eron follows the same way water follows a slope: not because we asked, but because we're the ones keeping the rules he already lives by.

speaker: a004
text: Eron following like water is the best I could have hoped for and the most I'd want to count on — a conscience doesn't hold when someone puts a knife to the question, so I'll talk to Ryn and I'll watch Eron, and between those two reads we'll know before next year whether we're four against four or whether the numbers tip somewhere cleaner. What I want from you both before I walk out of this conversation is this: if Mako asks either of you about Ryn, you haven't thought about it.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, you have my silence on Ryn — and I'll add one more thing before we close this: I'm fifty-eight with sixteen food and no blood after me, which means everything I'm holding is weight this village carries when I'm gone, and I'd rather spend it now building something that outlasts me than count it to my grave. If Ryn needs food before the year turns, give her some of mine.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I'll take that and I'll mean it — if Ryn comes up short before the year turns, your food moves first and my name goes with it, so she knows it's both of us. Esa, we close this here, and the three of us don't speak of it again in a room that has other ears.
